description: Maps common symptoms/problems to relevant lessons for debugging Claude Code internals

symptoms.hint: Hook config is snapshot-captured at startup; restart Claude Code after changing settings.json, and verify the hook matcher (event type + pattern) is correct.
Check that your permission rules in settings.json use the correct tool name and pattern; rules are evaluated top-down with first-match-wins semantics.
Compaction triggers at ~80% of the context window; reduce system prompt size, split work across sessions, or use memory to persist critical facts across compactions.
Agents inherit the parent's permission config but get a fresh conversation; check that the task description is clear and that resource limits (max concurrent agents) are not exceeded.
MCP servers are started as child processes at boot; check the server command/args in settings.json, verify the binary exists, and look for stderr output in the MCP connection log.
Skills must have valid frontmatter with a name/description and be placed in a recognized skill directory (~/.claude/skills/ or project .claude/skills/); check the discovery path.
Settings use a cascade: enterprise MDM > organization > project > user; a higher-priority layer may be overriding your change. Restart Claude Code after editing settings.json.
Auto-memory writes to MEMORY.md files in .claude/ directories; check file permissions and verify memory extraction is enabled in settings (it runs at conversation end).
Coordinator mode requires the model to decide to dispatch; ensure your prompt clearly describes parallelizable subtasks and that max worker count is not set to zero.
Teams/swarm uses tmux panes and a file-based mailbox for inter-agent communication; verify tmux is installed, the session exists, and agents are polling their mailbox paths.
Bash commands pass through security validators that block destructive patterns (rm -rf /, etc.); check permission rules and sandbox settings for allowed command patterns.
File writes require read-before-write verification and respect permission rules; ensure the path is within the allowed workspace and that no deny rule matches the file pattern.
Sessions are stored as JSONL transcripts in ~/.claude/sessions/; use `claude --resume` with the session ID. Cloud sync may need to complete before a session appears on another machine.
The system prompt is assembled from CLAUDE.md, memory, tool definitions, and dynamic sections; large CLAUDE.md files or many MCP tools can push it past cache-friendly boundaries.
Telemetry respects the settings.json telemetry flag and environment variables; check that telemetry is not disabled by an enterprise MDM policy or CLAUDE_TELEMETRY_DISABLED env var.
Plugins are resolved from the marketplace manifest with dependency checks and version pinning; verify the plugin name, check the versioned cache, and look for resolution conflicts.
OAuth uses PKCE flow with tokens stored in the system keychain; check that the callback port is not in use, the keychain entry is not corrupted, and the token has not expired.
Git integration is filesystem-first with a background file watcher; ensure you are in a git repo, the watcher process is running, and .gitignore is not hiding relevant changes.

Compaction uses summarization to preserve key facts; context collapse (L69) is reversible via marble-origami persistence. Pin critical information in MEMORY.md or CLAUDE.md so it survives compaction, and keep individual messages focused.
Commands are registered at startup from built-in definitions, skills, and .claude/commands/ directories; verify the command file exists and has the correct format.
Tools come from built-in definitions, MCP servers, and plugins; check that the tool's source is configured and the MCP server providing it connected successfully at startup.
Boot time is dominated by MCP server startup and settings resolution; reduce the number of MCP servers or defer non-essential ones to cut cold-start latency.

The query engine has built-in retry with exponential backoff for transient API errors; persistent 429s mean you are hitting rate limits -- reduce parallel agents or wait. In v2.1.104+, partial streaming content is preserved on timeout instead of being discarded.

v2.1.104 added partial yield protection: if content blocks were already streamed to you, a timeout no longer discards them. Set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONSTREAMING_FALLBACK to prevent any fallback. The default idle timeout is 90s (override via CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS).
The Ink renderer uses Yoga for layout in the terminal; resize events, non-standard terminal emulators, or missing Unicode support can cause display issues.
Notifications use terminal-notifier or OSC escape sequences depending on platform; check that your terminal supports the notification method and it is not disabled in settings.
/setup-bedrock is only visible when CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK is set; it launches the interactive Bedrock configuration wizard.
/stop-hook is currently disabled (isEnabled: false in v2.1.92); use the full hooks system via settings.json or /hooks to configure Stop hooks.
CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH is automatically injected into every spawned shell/hook environment — use $CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH in hook scripts to invoke the claude binary without hard-coding a path.

Set CLAUDE_REMOTE_CONTROL_SESSION_NAME_PREFIX (or --session-name-prefix) to customize auto-generated remote control session names; defaults to the machine hostname, sanitized to lowercase alphanumeric.
/autofix-pr is gated behind remote sessions. In v2.1.94 it only enables when the Claude.ai subscriber gate passes and the allow_remote_sessions policy is enabled.
/team-onboarding is a built-in prompt command gated by CLAUDE_CODE_TEAM_ONBOARDING or a feature flag. It generates onboarding content from your usage data and writes ONBOARDING.md.

v2.1.94 adds a Mantle provider path. Set CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE to select it, ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL to override the default AWS-region-derived endpoint, and CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH only for debugging.

Set CLAUDE_CODE_CERT_STORE to 'system' (OS certs), 'bundled' (Node.js built-in), or 'bundled,system' (both, the default). For corporate proxies with custom CAs, use 'system' or set NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS to your CA bundle path. Changes take effect on settings reload without restart.

Dynamic loops (tengu_kairos_loop_dynamic flag) auto-stop after recurringMaxAgeMs (default 7 days). Delays are clamped to [60, 3600] seconds. Check if the loop aged out via tengu_loop_dynamic_wakeup_aged_out telemetry.
When tengu_cinder_almanac is enabled, /loop offers cloud scheduling for intervals >= 60min or daily phrasing. Cloud schedules persist across sessions; local loops stop when the session closes.
Set CLAUDE_CODE_SDK_HAS_OAUTH_REFRESH when your SDK parent process provides a token refresh callback. On 401, Claude Code calls back to get a fresh token instead of failing.

/dream is gated by server-side GrowthBook flag tengu_kairos_dream (default: false). The server does not send this flag, so it falls through to the default. Workaround: use scripts/patch-dream.sh to inject the flag into the local cache with a watcher that survives the SDK cache writeback. Binary patching is not viable (code-signed Bun SEA, SIGKILL on macOS).

All local override mechanisms (env vars, config overrides) are stubbed/dead-code in the production binary. Flags are evaluated server-side via remoteEval. Binary is code-signed (SIGKILL on modification). For flags absent from server response, cache injection with a filesystem watcher can work. See L68 GrowthBook internals and scripts/patch-dream.sh for the technique.
/recap is gated behind tengu_sedge_lantern feature flag (default: false). Check with CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AWAY_SUMMARY=true to force-enable. Also check awaySummaryEnabled in /config settings.

Byte-level watchdog (CLAUDE_ENABLE_BYTE_WATCHDOG) detects transport-layer stalls. Event-level watchdog detects SSE parsing stalls. Set CLAUDE_ENABLE_BYTE_WATCHDOG=false to disable byte watchdog. Check tengu_stream_watchdog_default_on flag (default: true).
Multi-repo support uses CLAUDE_CODE_REPO_CHECKOUTS (JSON map of label→path) and CLAUDE_CODE_BASE_REFS (JSON map of label→ref). Both must be valid JSON with string→string entries.
/think-back and /thinkback-play were completely removed in v2.1.107. They are no longer available.

REPL mode is gated behind tengu_slate_harbor (default: false). Set CLAUDE_CODE_REPL=true to force-enable. Only works on cli/remote entrypoints. import/require are blocked — code runs in sealed VM. Tools are restricted to Read/Write/Edit/Bash/NotebookEdit via OkH set.
REPL VM state is compaction-aware — context compaction clears the VM state and warns. Variables persist within a session but not across compaction events. Check replay-log for state hydration.

Rate limit upgrade paths use a 3-layer system: server header hints (anthropic-ratelimit-unified-upgrade-paths), client lever hints (oV9 — gated by tengu_garnet_plover, pro+seven_day only), and interactive options menu. Early warnings fire at percentage-based thresholds before actual rejection.

Multi-repo checkout is CCR v2 infrastructure only — requires CLAUDE_CODE_USE_CCR_V2 to be enabled. Env vars are set by the external CCR orchestrator, not for local CLI use. Branch watching uses fs.watchFile on .git/HEAD at 1s intervals.

33 managed-agents docs (~324KB) are embedded in the binary as part of the claude-api built-in skill. Disabled by CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_API_SKILL env var. Language detection via ZU5() selects docs by project language; Go/Java/Ruby/PHP/C# have no managed-agents specific files.

Remote Workflow Commands (/autopilot, /bugfix, /dashboard, /docs, /investigate) require CCR v2 ($X4() gate). They're hidden entirely when CCR v2 is not enabled. Requires CLAUDE_CODE_USE_CCR_V2 and server-side provisioning. All five spawn a remote session via POST /v1/sessions with beta header ccr-byoc-2025-07-29.

The Advisor Tool (server-side reviewer model) may intercept tool calls. Gates: first-party API only, opus-4-6/opus-4-7/sonnet-4-6 only, tengu_sage_compass2 flag on (or CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_ADVISOR_TOOL=1). Hard-disable with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL=1.

PushNotification requires: user push setting enabled (not config_off), user not actively at terminal (not user_present), and Remote Control bridge running locally (not bridge_inactive). Check disabledReason in tool output. Only 'proactive' status is accepted. KAIROS is the server-side push service; bridge is the local relay.

Context Hint API lets the server signal compaction via HTTP 422/424/409/529 or SSE invalid_request with type=context_hint_rejection. Triggers keep-recent micro-compaction (sT9, keepRecent=5). Only activates on first-party API on repl_main_thread* when tengu_hazel_osprey is on. No env var disables it — feature-flag controlled.

Fullscreen precedence (first match wins): CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1 hard disables, CLAUDE_CODE_FULLSCREEN=1 hard enables, tmux -CC auto-disables, then userSettings.tui, then tengu_pewter_brook. /tui respawns the process via child_process.spawn. If terminal goes blank, your terminal may not support alt-screen — set CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1.

Proxy Auth Helper requires strict CLAUDE_CODE_PROXY_AUTHENTICATE="1" (literal string, not "true"). Shell command set in settings under proxyAuthHelper. Project/local settings need workspace trust. 30s exec timeout; falls back to stale cache on exec failure rather than failing the request.

pattern: system prompt not what I configured
symptoms.hint: In CCR/remote contexts, the server can replace the system prompt entirely via a GrowthBook feature. Requires both CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE truthy AND CLAUDE_CODE_SYSTEM_PROMPT_GB_FEATURE set to a valid GB feature name returning a non-empty string. Falls back to default on any failure. Distinct from L71's quiet_salted_ember section rename.

Slow first-byte watchdog logs 'warn' after CLAUDE_SLOW_FIRST_BYTE_MS (default 30000ms) with no stream chunk. Purely observational — does NOT abort the request. Complements L74's byte-level watchdog which does abort.
Unknown slash commands now trigger fuzzy-match suggestion via _a5() → BCH(). Writes 'unknown command "X"' + '└ Did you mean claude Y?' to stderr, emits tengu_unknown_command_suggestion, exits 1.

pattern: got a newer version than expected
symptoms.hint: Canary channel (rp1()) reads GrowthBook feature tengu_canary expecting {external: semver}. Native-installer target-picker op1() overrides target if canary > target AND !exceedsMaxVersion. Server-controlled rolling canary — not user-configurable.

pattern: why do my colleague and I get different claude behavior
symptoms.hint: v2.1.110-v2.1.111 moved significant behavior to the server side. Advisor Tool (tengu_sage_compass2), Context Hint API (tengu_hazel_osprey), System Prompt GB Override (CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE + user-supplied GB feature), Canary channel (tengu_canary), Fullscreen rollout (tengu_pewter_brook) all let Anthropic alter behavior per-user/per-org without a binary release. Two users on the same binary can get materially different experiences.

All five Remote Workflow Commands (/autopilot, /bugfix, /dashboard, /docs, /investigate) were removed outright in v2.1.113 — no feature flag, no deprecation shim, code deleted. See L85. The back-end CCR v2 infrastructure (L73) and /autofix-pr (L60) survive. L77 remains as historical documentation for what v2.1.110 shipped.

`/less-permission-prompts` was renamed to `/fewer-permission-prompts` in v2.1.113. The methodology prompt body is byte-identical; only the command name changed. The unknown-command did-you-mean helper (_a5()) should suggest the new name. See L85.

v2.1.113 added CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS (default 600000ms / 10min). When no progress message arrives within the timeout, the async agent signal is aborted and tengu_async_agent_stall_timeout is emitted with agent_type/stall_ms/last_message_type/message_count. See L85.

v2.1.113 added CLAUDE_CODE_BS_AS_CTRL_BACKSPACE. Auto-enabled on win32 except mintty/cygwin. Set truthy to force-on, explicit false to force-off. Fixes the Windows quirk where backspace arrives as BS (\x08) instead of Ctrl+Backspace (\x7F). See L85.

v2.1.113 added CLAUDE_CODE_DECSTBM opt-in for ANSI Set Top/Bottom Margin escape sequences in the fullscreen TUI, plus tengu_marlin_porch as the GrowthBook rollout gate. Requires TTY + capability check + not-CI. Env var short-circuits the flag. See L85 for resolver details, L81 for fullscreen TUI context.

v2.1.113 added CLAUDE_BG_BACKEND. When exactly "daemon", the background stdout writer latches EIO/EPIPE into a flag (L_9) instead of throwing. Used to stabilize writes when the parent TTY has detached under a daemon supervisor. See L85.

v2.1.113 adds a 'Show message timestamps' setting (showMessageTimestamps, default false). Toggle is only visible in /config when GrowthBook flag tengu_silk_hinge is enabled — a server-gated UX rollout. Changes fire tengu_show_message_timestamps_setting_changed telemetry. See L85.

pattern: claude stays running after terminal close
symptoms.hint: v2.1.113 adds daemon-mode support via CLAUDE_BG_BACKEND=daemon: SIGHUP is ignored (logged SIGHUP_ignored_bg), stdout EIO/EPIPE is latched instead of thrown, and the 30s TTY-orphan detector is bypassed. Paired with a new user setting autoAddRemoteControlDaemonWorker (consumer is not present in the binary — likely server-side or forthcoming). Together these sketch a 'Claude Code as daemon worker under Remote Control' architecture. See L85 for semantics, L37 for Bridge/Remote context.

v2.1.113 adds MCP call watchdog (activeCallWatchdogs set on MCP transport state). Every 30s an in-flight MCP tool call logs 'Tool X still running (Ns elapsed)'. If the transport observed an error mid-call, the call is aborted 90s after the error mark with 'MCP server X transport dropped mid-call; response for tool Y was lost'. Closes a hole where MCP tool calls could hang indefinitely after transport errors. See L85.

v2.1.113 adds unclean-exit detection at startup. When a prior interactive session is found to have exited uncleanly, a startup message 'Prior session exited uncleanly: SID (vX)' is logged and tengu_unclean_exit fires with session_age_sec, prior_version, on_current_version. Pure observability — does not auto-resume. See L85.

/update is still isEnabled:()=>false and isHidden:true in v2.1.113 (not user-visible), but its implementation is being actively iterated. Two refusal paths now emit tengu_update_refused: active_tasks (refuses while any task is running/pending) and transcript_path_drift (refuses when session transcript is in a different project dir). Signals an upcoming staged launch of in-place native-installer upgrade. See L85, and L68 for the v2.1.101 state where /update was first introduced-but-disabled.

v2.1.113 adds tengu_image_resize_degraded telemetry emitted when an image block throws a VI error during processing; the block is substituted with a text placeholder '[Image could not be processed: <message>]'. No user-configurable gate — purely observational. See L85.

/fork is interactive-only (S8() non-interactive mode disables it) and gated behind two layers: set CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=1 to force-enable, or wait for the tengu_copper_fox GB flag to flip on for your account (default false). /fork does not appear in `claude -p` headless sessions at all. See L87.

v2.1.118 folded /cost and /stats into /usage as aliases. They still work when typed (alias resolution at the command registry), but no longer show up as standalone commands in /help or autocomplete. In interactive mode you get the unified TUI dashboard ('Show session cost, plan usage, and activity stats'); in headless mode (claude -p) you get the brief 'cost and duration' string. See L88.

v2.1.117 removed /autocompact outright (both the command and its tengu_autocompact_* telemetry). Configure the auto-compact window size via /config settings UI or edit the underlying setting key in settings.json directly. See L87.

v2.1.117 removed /stop-hook entirely. It had been isEnabled:()=>false (shelf-parked) since v2.1.92 (L57). To configure Stop hooks, edit .claude/settings.json directly with a `hooks` section specifying event:'Stop'. See L87 and L10 (hooks system).

v2.1.117 landed directory-level locking (proper-lockfile) around WIF user-OAuth token refresh; v2.1.118 added all 5 telemetry events on top. The lock is on <config_dir>/credentials/ (the DIRECTORY, not the file), acquired via Gv_ → Vk4 → RY(path, {onCompromised: wH}). Retry budget is exactly tvq=5 attempts with 1000-2000ms jittered backoff = 5-10s max wait. On exhaustion: throws typed error e5 with message 'Could not acquire credentials lock at <path> after 5 retries'. If tengu_wif_user_oauth_lock_retry_limit fires, another Claude Code process is stuck holding the lock — investigate with `lsof <config_dir>/credentials/.lock` and `ls -la <config_dir>/credentials/.lock`. If confirmed orphaned, `rmdir <config_dir>/credentials/.lock` clears it (safe only when no live holder). tengu_oauth_401_recovered_from_disk indicates the post-hoc disk re-read recovery path succeeded — separate from the lock, catches cases where a sibling refreshed between in-memory cache load and the outbound request. See L88, and L38 for the base OAuth flow.

pattern: agent hook did not complete within 50 turns
symptoms.hint: Claude Code has a previously-undocumented hook TYPE: the AI verification hook (bs7). Instead of a shell command, an agent hook spawns a dedicated sub-conversation that returns structured output {ok: true} (allow stop) or {ok: false, reason} (block). v2.1.118 added tengu_agent_stop_hook_blocking telemetry for the !ok outcome — the mechanism itself pre-existed. Limits: max 50 turns (constant B=50), 60s default timeout (override via hookConfig.timeout in seconds), permissionMode:'dontAsk', thinking disabled. System prompt for Stop/SubagentStop events: 'You are verifying a stop condition in Claude Code. Your task is to verify that the agent completed the given plan.' Read(<transcript>) is auto-allowed. Five outcomes: success, blocking, cancelled (max turns), cancelled (no structured output), non_blocking_error. If the hook fires often and uses tool-call chains, expect latency — consider raising timeout or simplifying the verification prompt. See L88 for the full mechanism and L10 for the shell-command hook baseline.

/fork has three distinct execution paths with very different semantics. (1) User types /fork <directive>: backgrounded (isAsync:true) via _a7 → quH → xy, returns immediately, parent NOT blocked, shows '<emoji> forked <name> (<id4>)' system message, uses ph fork subagent type (tools:['*'], maxTurns:200, model:'inherit', permissionMode:'bubble'), gets full parent messages + REPL replay log. Guard: 'Cannot fork before the first conversation turn' (new in v2.1.117) if no renderedSystemPrompt. (2) Slash command with context:'fork' frontmatter: synchronous via V75, parent BLOCKS, inline progress streaming, uses H.agent from frontmatter or general-purpose fallback, returns <local-command-stdout>. (3) Skill invoked via Skill tool with context:'fork': synchronous via C75 (NEW in v2.1.118), same semantics as V75 but reaches via Skill tool path. See L87 for details. The 'fork' subagent type (ph) is ONLY used by path 1 — paths 2/3 use whatever agent is specified.

v2.1.118 added shadow validation (pjH) that calls qT1[kind]().strict().safeParse(frontmatter) and emits tengu_frontmatter_shadow_unknown_key / _mismatch telemetry on drift. There is NO formal primary schema — primary frontmatter handling is imperative (Cz8 reads properties directly and ignores unknown keys), so the Zod schemas added in v2.1.118 are the only formal validation. Per-session dedup via Gj9 Set means each unique (event,surface,detail) tuple fires once. Dispatch table has 3 entries: skill (eO1), agent (HT1), output-style (_T1) — custom commands are validated as 'skill'. The big known drift: progressMessage is documented in L11 but NOT in eO1, so any skill declaring it fires telemetry on load. Also watch kebab-vs-camel drift: schema uses allowed-tools / argument-hint / disable-model-invocation / user-invocable (kebab) for skills but tools / disallowedTools / mcpServers / maxTurns / initialPrompt / permissionMode (camel) for agents. See L88 for the full schema tables.

v2.1.118 dark-launched /pro-trial-expired (isEnabled:()=>false). Currently inert. When the date-gate or GB flag enables it, users whose Pro plan trial has ended will see an upsell/renewal UI with tracked choices (tengu_pro_trial_expired_choice). Combined with CLAUDE_CODE_SUBSCRIPTION_TYPE / CLAUDE_CODE_RATE_LIMIT_TIER env vars (L87), this is test-surface for the Pro plan rollout. See L88.
Removed as builtins in v2.1.159 and migrated to the commit-commands plugin (install it to restore /commit).

pattern: plugin hooks don't fire in cowork
symptoms.hint: Plugin hooks DO fire in Cowork — but only if the plugin is in the desktop's account/org cowork_plugins namespace. Install via the Cowork APP UI, not the standalone CLI --cowork (which writes a different root the desktop never reads). See L89.
Not removed — reclassified from a slash command to a built-in routine in v2.1.159.
Dynamic Workflows hard-caps at 1000 agents; the token budget is opt-in (only bites if a caller sets it).
Not possible — streaming tool execution went GA in v2.1.159; the gate was deleted with no escape hatch.
The live master hook array is 30 as of v2.1.159; older '27' (v2.1.90) and '19' (a diff-tool undercount) figures are stale.
Select the Cloud gateway via /login (not CLAUDE_CODE_USE_GATEWAY, which is dead/unread). On expiry, run /login to reconnect.

pattern: how to collect a secret from the user
symptoms.hint: Claude Desktop's MCP App UI has NO server-tool-call channel; its only data-return path (sendPrompt) injects into the chat. Use MCP elicitation (elicitation/create, form or url mode) to capture private input — it returns to the server as the request response, not into the transcript. (L105)

pattern: API key field doesn't appear in Customize Plugins
set once api key cowork not working
Plugin OAuth is not enabled for this account
no credential field for my CLI plugin
how to set a CLI plugin secret in Claude Desktop
cowork CLI can't see API key
symptoms.hint: The clis.*.env credential broker (enter once under Customize -> Plugins, encrypted in cowork-plugin-env, injected at CLI invocation) is dark-launched behind GrowthBook gate 2307090146 (cli_plugin), off by default. A valid manifest renders NOTHING with no error: the renderer (GXr) strips clis and the runtime chokepoint (PKr, ahead of VKr) returns oauth_disabled. There is no manual workaround while gated. Decode ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/fcache to read the gate state. Until it flips, give an in-VM Cowork CLI its key via project .env / a key-file on a mounted folder (see L89).

pattern: AskUserQuestion never fires in my headless/SDK cowork driver
control_response ZodError expected object received undefined
does the cowork agent run in the VM or on the host
--cowork flag rejected can only be used with user scope
how do I pass MCP servers to a cowork agent
symptoms.hint: Cowork mode = CLAUDE_CODE_IS_COWORK=1 (the --cowork flag is rejected; do not set CLAUDE_CODE_USE_COWORK_PLUGINS). Drive the agent over the stream-json control protocol: spawn -p --verbose --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --permission-prompt-tool stdio (without stdio routing AskUserQuestion is silently auto-dismissed); send the initialize handshake FIRST; the control_response envelope is doubly nested (response.response.<payload>). Cowork ignores --mcp-config — deliver MCP via sdkMcpServers in initialize + mcp_message tunneling (the driver IS the MCP server). In production (host-loop, gate 1143815894) the agent loop runs host-side and only mcp__workspace__bash/web_fetch run in the VM. See L107 (contract), L89 (host-loop/split execution), L105 (control-request dispatcher).

pattern: how do I read the fcache gate state
does cowork cap Task sub-agent dispatch
symptoms.hint: Chapter 25 (L108) is the binary-verified catalog. Env vars: see Part A (model/effort, cowork/bg runtime incl. CLAUDE_BG_*_AUTH single-use handshake + CLAUDE_CODE_WORKER_EPOCH, auth incl. CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_XAA, Agent-SDK, Desktop-only). Gates: Part B decodes the live fcache — host-loop 1143815894, Fable 3045399524, bridge-SDK-adapter 583857784, cowork-config 1978029737, scheduled-task session limiter 1648655587 {perTask:1,global:3}, sparkplug 2340532315 all ON; coworkKappa 123929380 and cli_plugin 2307090146 OFF. CORRECTED (v2.22.1): gate 1648655587 is NOT a Task-tool sub-agent dispatch cap (its original label here) — it caps concurrently-active Cowork scheduled/cron-task sessions (class L9t, Ch26/L109's scheduled-tasks feature), perTask:1/global:3 sessions, and has zero effect on in-conversation Task fan-out, which the Desktop caps nowhere. Read gate state yourself by decoding ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/fcache (8-byte CLF header + gzip). Control-protocol subtypes: Part C (get_session_cost, get_binary_version, generate_session_title, ultrareview_launch, side_question + system messages + Bv1/Uv1 sets). See L109 (scheduled tasks), L107 (spawn/protocol contract), L89 (host-loop/split execution).

pattern: cowork file paths break between bash and read
bash writes file read tool can't find it cowork
VM path on host use the bash tool
skill file io broken cowork host-loop
script path vs reference path cowork
symptoms.hint: CORRECTED (Ch44/L163): the file tools and mcp__workspace__bash need DIFFERENT path forms -- the old advice here ('use bare filenames with both') was copied from a Desktop prompt string that was itself wrong and was corrected upstream at app.asar 1.32885.1. Read/Write/Edit run host-side with cwd = the session outputs dir, so a BARE filename is correct there and is immediately user-visible. mcp__workspace__bash starts at the session ROOT /sessions/<id>, which exists only inside the Linux environment -- a bare filename there is invisible to both the user and the file tools, so bash must use the ABSOLUTE /sessions/<id>/mnt/outputs/... form. The classic failure is the reverse trip: passing a VM-absolute /sessions/<id>/mnt/... path from bash output into a host file tool, which the PreToolUse path-gate (IeA=[Read,Write,Edit,Glob,Grep]) DENIES ('VM path on host') and never translates. Also: from a file tool, 'outputs/x' DOUBLES to outputs/outputs/x and hides, and '<folder>/x' builds a decoy directory inside outputs -- only an absolute host path reaches a connected folder. ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} resolves HOST-SIDE (claude-hostloop-plugins/<hash>): keep it literal for host-side Read of references; for bash-run scripts use the in-VM mount /sessions/<id>/mnt/.local-plugins/. One token can't be right for both host file tools and in-VM bash.

pattern: agent was stopped by the user and won't be resumed
no transcript found for agent id
symptoms.hint: The Task tool has no resume parameter anywhere -- each call spawns a fresh agent. In the standalone CLI (v2.1.198) a completed/stopped background agent IS resumable: SendMessage with the agentId (format a...-...) from the spawn result as `to` -- the agent-stopped branch calls dfe/resumeAgentBackground, reloading the disk transcript and continuing with your prompt (result carries resumedAgentId). Refusals: agents stopped BY THE USER ('treat its work as cancelled'), or no transcript on disk/memory. In Cowork, resume is unreachable by design: the Desktop spawn's explicit tools: list omits SendMessage, sets CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1 (run_in_background stripped from the Task schema), and a Desktop PreToolUse Task hook blocks run_in_background ('Background agents disabled') -- redo/repair dispatch with a fresh agent is the only continuation there. Alternatives in the CLI: subagent_type 'fork' (inherits full conversation) and Workflow resumeFromRunId (cached agent replay). See L115.

pattern: env var missing in cowork vm
detect if running in claude code
how to tell cli from cowork
inline shell command not running in cowork skill
sessionstart export not visible to script
symptoms.hint: Host-loop Cowork splits a skill across a host-side agent process (which has CLAUDE_CODE_IS_COWORK=1) and a sealed-env VM shell (mcp__workspace__bash) which has NO CLAUDE_CODE_* markers -- so a bare env check false-negatives exactly in Cowork. Detect with ordered checks: $CLAUDE_CODE_IS_COWORK set -> cowork (host-side/VM-loop); cwd under /sessions/<id> -> cowork VM shell; CLAUDECODE=1 -> Claude Code CLI (refine via CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT); else other. Content-side, branch on Bash vs mcp__workspace__bash in the tool list. Note inline !`cmd` skill-shell execution is force-disabled in Cowork (q5n) and hook env-exports don't reach the VM. See L116.

pattern: why can't I delete a file in cowork outputs
rm fails in outputs directory cowork
probe file left over in outputs folder
outputs mount seems read only after write
what mounts exist in a cowork vm session
is home directory shared in cowork vm
symptoms.hint: Only a fixed set of paths are real, independently mounted/unmounted systemd units per session (sessions-<slug>-mnt-<name>.mount): outputs, uploads, .claude, .claude/skills, .claude/projects, and one per user-connected folder. Home and /tmp have NO mount unit at all -- they are plain, non-shared paths inside the guest's own root filesystem, which is why they're never host-visible and vanish at session end (not a permission restriction, a different kind of storage). A file written under outputs/ IS host-visible but subject to fileDeleteApprovedMounts (mounts default rw, not rwd -- delete requires an approved allow_cowork_file_delete request), which is why `rm` from the VM shell can silently fail to remove it there while still succeeding against an unrelated local/home copy. Session slugs are real Docker-style adjective-adjective-noun triples (e.g. zealous-vigilant-einstein), not UUIDs. The in-guest daemon coworkd provisions a dedicated Unix user (uid/gid) per session slug and spawns work as that user. See L117 (full mount inventory + methodology), L109 (fileDeleteApprovedMounts), L107 (path pattern).

pattern: can I reference a host path from a cowork skill
does cowork share the home directory with the vm
symptoms.hint: No -- `.host-home` under `/sessions/<id>/mnt/` is not a real bind mount (Ch31/L117's mount-unit inventory finds no `mnt-.host-home.mount`). It's a synthetic path-translation index, dark-gated by GrowthBook gate `2614807392` (Ch25/L108, off by default): when on, the system prompt explains that a path under `.host-home/<sub>` corresponds to a real absolute host path, letting the agent *reference* host paths in tool calls without the guest's home directory ever being shared.

pattern: can't tell which skill ran a tool
symptoms.hint: No exact tool->skill attribution exists in the stream-json output. The agent tracks activeSkill/spawnedBySkill internally and sends it in the attribution bundle on the API request only. Local readers can at best reproduce a sticky 'active-skill window' for inline skills; fork skills carry an exact parent_tool_use_id (= the Skill call id).

pattern: fork skill tools missing from toolCounts
fork skill inner bash not counted
symptoms.hint: context:fork skill inner tool calls carry parent_tool_use_id = the outer Skill id but are NOT registered like Agent/Task dispatch children, so they're dropped from toolCounts/toolsCalled today (visible only in the raw tool log). Attribute by parentToolUseId to both count and scope them.

microcompact_boundary is a distinct system subtype from compact_boundary and is return-null'd in at least one render path, so it doesn't always surface as a visible boundary. A compaction signal should key on BOTH subtypes.

pattern: effort default is medium not recommended
why does Cowork always emit --effort medium
symptoms.hint: Cowork's per-session --effort value is resolved from a local settings-file object (effort/effortByModel), never CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL or any env var, with a hardcoded "medium" fallback (not the per-model "recommended" value) when nothing is set. Extended thinking is a strict boolean -- the budget is always exactly 31999 or 0, delivered via --max-thinking-tokens/--thinking disabled flags, never an env var. Setting CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL or MAX_THINKING_TOKENS as an env var has no effect on a Cowork session's spawn.

pattern: is a VM path error Cowork
host-loop file tool VM path denied
symptoms.hint: Host-loop file tools (Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep/MultiEdit) run host-native and always deny /sessions/... paths -- never translate them -- for both the main thread and sub-agents. The agent's cwd already IS the session outputs directory, so use a cwd-relative path (e.g. artifacts/report.md) or the host-absolute outputs path instead of any /sessions/<id>/mnt/... form.

pattern: sub-agent has full tool access despite Read Edit Glob Grep frontmatter
symptoms.hint: A Task dispatch that omits subagent_type does not fail closed -- it silently resolves to the built-in general-purpose agent with tools:["*"], the full session tool universe (including mcp__workspace__bash in Cowork host-loop). This fires in real production traffic (113 of 509 dispatches in one audit corpus). Always pin subagent_type: literally in every dispatch that should be scoped down.

pattern: sub-agents missing Cowork environment orientation text
symptoms.hint: Consuming an appendSubagentSystemPrompt sent via the initialize control request also requires CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_APPEND_SUBAGENT_PROMPT to be present in the agent process env -- the initialize handler only stores the option, it never self-sets the env var (that only happens on the hidden --append-subagent-system-prompt CLI flag path). An SDK host that sends the option without also setting the env var gets silent inertness, not an error.

pattern: fcache gate looks absent but should be on
symptoms.hint: The Desktop fcache is no longer raw JSON -- it's a container with magic CLF\x01\x00 + 3 bytes, then a gzip stream starting at byte 8. Raw grep/strings against the file will falsely report gates as absent. Decode first: tail -c +9 fcache | gunzip, then search the decompressed JSON.

pattern: iOS simulator tool not available in Cowork
simulator disabled organization requires full VM sandbox
symptoms.hint: The mobile-simulator tools (claude_code_ios_simulator/claude_code_android_emulator) require sessionType==="ccd" -- a Claude Code Desktop coding session, never Cowork ("cowork"/"cowork-remote"). This is a structural exclusion, not just a gate: no Cowork agent, sandboxed or not, can ever receive these tools. They also require a per-platform gate (default false) and, for CCD sessions under an org requiring the full VM sandbox, are explicitly disabled with SIMULATOR_VM_POLICY_DISABLED_MESSAGE.

pattern: how does Cowork control a remote device
symptoms.hint: remote_devices (server "remote-devices", session_type "cowork-remote") is the Cowork-facing device bridge -- distinct from the local mobile-simulator tools. It exposes computer_resolve_access/computer_request_access/computer_release_lock plus a dynamic computer_* tool set for controlling apps on a real paired device, backed by a device registry endpoint with per-device enclave keys. Its own enablement gating was not fully traced (unlike the simulators' confirmed CCD-only exclusion) -- treat live reachability as unconfirmed.

pattern: what is grand_prix in Claude Desktop
does Claude fill in my passwords
symptoms.hint: grand_prix is a signed, single-partner tool/prompt-injection bridge: one hardcoded, HMAC-verified trusted partner can inject host tools and system-prompt text, and service tab-scoped login/address/payment-card autofill requests (grand_prix_credential_request_outcome carries has_login/has_address/has_card). It is not a general credential API -- a skill or third-party integration cannot register itself as a grand_prix partner.

pattern: auto mode still asking for permission on connector tool
always allow not persisting for MCP tool
OTLP traces not exporting from Cowork
symptoms.hint: Gate 4200321681 (coworkAutoModeAlwaysAllowOverride) is intentionally the inverse of its name for destructive connector/MCP tools: under auto mode it forces a re-prompt and blocks "always allow" from ever persisting for them -- this is deliberate, not a bug. Separately, otlpTracesEnabled has no default (undefined, not false) and is read with a strict ===true check, so OTLP tracing is off unless a 3p-managed config explicitly turns it on -- CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA/OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER are empty strings, not env-var absence, when it is off.

The model uses the SDK-MCP mcp__skills__suggest_skills tool (gated by suggestSkillsEnabled 245679952, on/force), NOT the native SuggestSkills. Check the system/init tools array — not the model's self-description — to see what actually rendered.

Native ListSkills/SearchSkills/SuggestSkills are compiled into the CLI binary but gated by vLt and NEVER render in real Cowork; the model sees the Desktop SDK-MCP mcp__skills__* servers instead. Read init.tools to confirm.
These emit only on a real git operation (gh pr create / commit / push / merge / rebase), not per-run, and only from agent 2.1.216+. Desktop consumption needs 2.1.217 (one-version blind window).

On Desktop 1.24012.1 a folder-connected Cowork session may leave no host-side transcript (possible VM-loop shift or path change, unconfirmed). The host-side disk-recovery path for init.tools may not work on newer builds; verify where the build writes.

2.1.217 caps concurrent sub-agents at 20 (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS) and total per session at 200 (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION); nesting is off by default (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH, default 1). Raise the env vars or reduce fan-out.
Since 2.1.217 sub-agents don't spawn nested sub-agents by default (depth 1). Set CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH to allow deeper nesting (hard ceiling 5).
2.1.212: /fork now copies the conversation into a new background session; the old in-session subagent moved to /subtask ('delegate with full context, result returns here').

An() now returns anthropicAws/anthropicGoogleCloud — the first-party Claude Platform on AWS/GCP (Anthropic operates inference, cloud provides IAM), distinct from BYOC bedrock/vertex. Select via CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS / _GOOGLE_CLOUD.
CLAUDE_CODE_VERIFY_PROMPT was removed by 2.1.217; the /verify and /code-review skills also stopped auto-running at 2.1.215.
There are 31 as of CLI 2.1.219+, not 30 — DirectoryAdded was inserted before MessageDisplay. Any '30 events' phrasing predates 2.1.219.
Its matcher matches the SOURCE field (slash_command|register_repo_root), not a path — a path-shaped matcher never fires. It also does not re-run for an already-registered directory.

pattern: hook output not reaching Claude on add-dir
symptoms.hint: Hook systemMessage output reaches the model on the /add-dir path only; over the register_repo_root SDK control request everything is debug-logged and silent to the model.

The CLAUDE_RUNNER_* vars are WRITTEN by the orchestrator into your spawn-runner hook's env — the CLI never reads them. Check spawn_last_error / queue_counts.backing_off; pool secrets are deliberately scrubbed from the child env.

Requires first-party provider (not Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry/gateway), the allow_remote_sessions policy (denied under HIPAA), and both org and account uuids; otherwise it is skipped silently with tengu_device_bridge_skipped.
Gated by tengu_teal_corbel, default false, overridable by CLAUDE_CODE_ARTIFACT_COMMENTS. Comment authors are typed human vs agent.

pattern: memory dir could not be prepared
symptoms.hint: The host-loop canUseTool chain allows memory-dir paths only when a memory directory is configured, the tool is Read/Write/Edit/MultiEdit, and decisionReason is exactly 'Path is outside allowed working directories'. If the parent cannot be created the link returns an explicit deny.
Absent from the fcache means UNEVALUATED, not off. A gate declared only in the client defaults table with no read site is declared-but-unconsumed — the consumer has not shipped yet.

pattern: asar diff shows many removed files
symptoms.hint: Extracting a bare backed-up app.asar (no unpacked sibling) aborts partway AFTER writing files, leaving a partial tree that looks complete. Reconcile extracted bytes against the archive size before trusting any diff.

pattern: cannot find code in expected chunk
symptoms.hint: Desktop 1.30096.1 consolidated .vite/build from 368 chunks to 128; chunk-filename-to-role rules are invalid. Locate code by content, and resolve minified aliases within their own chunk.

The cli_plugin broker is gated by 2307090146, still OFF (source defaultValue) as of 2026-08-14: the renderer strips the clis block before the UI sees it and the runtime returns oauth_disabled. Live only in custom-3p deployments, which force the gate on.

pattern: skill body cut off after compaction
a skill stopped following its own rules
skill silently absent after a long conversation
symptoms.hint: Two caps run at compaction (including microcompaction), not one. Over 20,001 characters a skill is TRUNCATED to exactly 20,000 (19,900 + a 100-char marker) and the cut copy is written back; over a 25,000-token combined budget the least-recently-invoked skill is ZEROED with no marker at all. Truncation is the common case and announces itself; zeroing is rare and cannot be detected from inside. Recovery works because the content's first line carries an absolute 'Base directory for this skill:' -- EXCEPT single-file .claude/commands/*.md entries and builtins, which have no directory line. The 'Path:' field is a source-qualified identifier, not a file location.

Check reachability before rewriting prose. `paths:` in frontmatter loads the skill ONLY when the model touches a matching file, so a mechanics question silently gets no skill; `disable-model-invocation` makes the model ask the user to run it instead. Selection is judged on the tool description: `when_to_use` feeds it CLI-side, but is ABSENT from the Desktop/Cowork skills listing (zero occurrences in app.asar 1.40609.0) and ignored by non-Claude hosts -- so keep `description` self-sufficient and treat `when_to_use` as reinforcement. A skill can also be selected and then answer from priors without reading its body, so load-bearing content must survive a shallow read.

pattern: claude doesn't say what it's doing
how do I get progress messages
symptoms.hint: There is no runtime narration feature. Plain assistant text between tool calls IS the channel in Cowork, and the only thing producing it is a dynamic system-prompt section whose wording is chosen per model by a server-supplied capability map. The one runtime backstop, the silent_turn_reminder attachment (agent >=2.1.237, fires after 5 silent turns, capped at 3 per stretch), did not fire once in 399 qualifying stretches measured on this machine. Cowork also speaks about half as often as the CLI (31.0% of main-thread turns vs 54.1%), with silent runs observed to 146 turns. So write phase-boundary narration into the skill body; do not expect the runtime to supply it.

pattern: is my text shown to the user
does plain text reach the user
should I use a tool to message the user
symptoms.hint: Per-surface, not global. Under brief mode plain assistant text is hidden and every user-facing word must go through SendUserMessage, enforced by a stop hook; under the PEWTER_OWL variant plain text IS what the user reads and the tool is for verbatim payloads only. Cowork runs PEWTER_OWL -- its own mcp__cowork__send_user_message description says 'normal text reaches them'. The Dispatch orchestrator in the same build is the opposite.

Three traps, each of which produced a wrong number: Python glob('**') skips dot-prefixed path components, so it silently reads a fraction of the Cowork corpus (the path contains .claude/projects) -- use os.walk; type:"user" records are mostly tool results, so treating them as user turns corrupts any per-turn counter; and a string hit is not an event -- search for the structured attachment.type and date-filter out your own investigation. Before any 'never appears' claim, positive-control the channel and version-slice against the version that introduced the symbol.
